lyrics:
[Intro: phone message beep, a grown child's voice, then synth riff]
Dad, it's me. You don't have to pick up.
Just checking.

[Verse 1: light, airy, driving drums and bass]
Hanging pictures on a nail that isn't there
Talking to the kettle and the stairs
Same key, same door, same number on the gate
Everything's in place and nothing's straight

[Chorus: chiming synth riff answers each line]
Same house, new weather
Same street, different sky
You'd know it and you wouldn't
And neither would I
Same house, new weather

[Verse 2: light, a little lower]
Kids call Sundays, ask me if I'm fine
I say the garden's good, I say I'm sleeping right
Your side of the closet, my side of the bed
All the words I've got are words you said

[Chorus: chiming synth riff answers each line]
Same house, new weather
Same street, different sky
You'd know it and you wouldn't
And neither would I
Same house, new weather

[Bridge: fast patter, drums pushing, one breath]
Bins on Thursday, pills at eight, the neighbour's dog, the garden gate
Your handwriting on every jar, the radio still in your car
I leave it, I leave it, I leave it where you are

[Final Chorus: full band, tubular bells on top]
Same house, new weather
Same street, different sky
You'd know it and you wouldn't
And neither would I
Same house, new weather

[Outro: tubular bells, synth riff, phone ringing, picked up]
Hi. Yeah. I'm here.
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 174 BPM, 4/4, A major. Fast, bright and light on its feet. It sounds like running and feels like standing still.

VOICE: Male tenor, light, airy and close, with no strain. He sings quietly even though the track is fast, and uses a soft falsetto on the ends of lines. The bridge is a quick, rhythmic patter in one breath. Spoken voices at the start and end.

INSTRUMENTS: A bright, chiming synthesiser playing a short riff like a music box crossed with a 1985 keyboard. A fast, steady live drum beat. A melodic, picked bass guitar. Jangling clean guitar. Soft pads. Tubular bells ringing out in the last chorus. Phone sounds.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, a message beep, two spoken lines, then the riff. 0:13 Verse 1. 0:35 Chorus 1. 0:57 Verse 2. 1:19 Chorus 2. 1:41 Bridge, fast patter. 1:58 Final chorus with tubular bells. 2:20 The riff and bells play out. 2:38 Outro, a phone rings and is answered, three spoken words at 2:48.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Early-2020s indie pop with a 1980s gloss: bright, tight and airy, drums dry, synth and bells shining on top.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The synth riff entering under the voicemail at 0:07.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The original is a young man's loneliness. Here the voice message is from a grown child, the house is a long marriage's house, and in the last three seconds he answers the phone.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Numb routine, missing someone, a rush of small memories, picking up.
